No infobox area on the Baden page; the only figure is about 3,500 km2 for the 1789 margraviate (ratio 2.1, plausible after the 1803 gains, the mediatisation page says 'Baden received over seven times as much', the comparison being left unstated). ledger.note: 1803: the Imperial Recess makes Baden an electorate under Charles Frederick. 'In 1803, the Imperial diet bestowed the office of Prince-elector to Charles Frederick'; the Recess page says 'Baden, Hesse-Kassel, and Württemberg gained status by being made electorates' and that it 'became law on 27 April' (month taken from that page). The Baden page gives only the year.

region.text: the Bishopric of Constance and the abbeys of Petershausen and Salem, with the imperial cities of Überlingen and Pfullendorf, on and around Lake Constance

ledger.note: 1803: Baden takes the Constance lands. Baden received ecclesiastical territory 'including Constance' and the abbeys of Petershausen and Salem, and the imperial cities of Überlingen and Pfullendorf (tables of the page); the Baden page: 'the Bishopric of Constance'. The region is a 40 km circle round Konstanz: the pages name the lands, not a boundary.

region.text: the right bank of the Speyer bishopric: Bruchsal and Odenheim

ledger.note: 1803: the Speyer lands on the right bank. The Recess tables give Baden 'the right bank of Speyer' with Odenheim and Bruchsal. A 20 km circle at Bruchsal is a placement: the page draws no line.

region.text: the right bank of the Strasbourg bishopric, the abbey of Gengenbach and the imperial cities of Offenburg and Zell am Harmersbach

ledger.note: 1803: the Strasbourg lands on the right bank. The tables give Baden 'the right bank of ... Strasbourg', the abbey of Gengenbach and the imperial cities Offenburg and Zell am Harmersbach (the last three had no owner of their own in Cliopatria and are counted here). A 25 km circle at Offenburg is a placement.

union.text: the imperial city of Biberach an der Riß

region.text: the Lordship of Schliengen (from Basel) and the imperial cities of Biberach an der Riß and Wimpfen

ledger.note: 1803: Schliengen. The tables give Baden 'the Lordship of Schliengen (from Basel)' and the imperial cities Biberach and Wimpfen; the Basel bishopric has no dossier, so the counterpart is the minor-states row. A 10 km circle only. [Reviewer eu-20-c, 2026-10-31: Biberach and Wimpfen, which this note names from the page's table 3 ('Biberach an der Riß; ... Wimpfen' under Baden), were missing from the region and lie outside the Cliopatria shape (east of 8.78 E); added as coordinate circles. Wimpfen's fate after 1803 is not on the page.]

region.text: part of the Electorate of the Palatinate

ledger.note: 1803: a slice of the Palatinate. Charles Frederick 'received the Bishopric of Constance, part of the Electorate of the Palatinate, and other smaller districts'. The page does not locate the Palatine part; the right-bank Palatinate round Heidelberg is the reading. The electoral-palatinate dossier ends in 1777 with Bavaria as successor, so the counterpart is duchy-of-bavaria, whose Cliopatria row ends in 1805.

region.text: Breisgau and other territories at the expense of the Austrian Empire

ledger.note: 26 December 1805: Pressburg gives Baden Breisgau (the further-austria dossier carries the loss). 'Charles Frederick obtained Breisgau and other territories at the expense of the Austrian Empire' (Baden page); the Pressburg page: the Austrian Swabian holdings passed to 'the King of Württemberg, and the Elector of Baden'; the War of the Third Coalition page dates the treaty 26 December 1805. The land enters the Grand Duchy's 1806 shape, not the Electorate's 1805 one. The Freiburg circle is a rough placement of the Breisgau; the pages do not list the other territories or draw the line between the Baden and Württemberg shares.

region.text: the Electorate of Baden, enlarged at Pressburg

ledger.note: 1805/1806: the Electorate becomes the sovereign Grand Duchy. 'In 1806 ... Francis II dissolved the Empire' and Baden 'declared sovereignty', Charles Frederick becoming Grand Duke; the electoral rank, a creature of the Empire, ends with it. The year 1806 is the page's; the dossier closes at Cliopatria's 1805 end so the Grand Duchy row can start in 1806.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition

zones.text: Breisgau and the other Austrian Swabian holdings passed to Baden and Württemberg at Pressburg

wars.outcome: French victory; the Peace of Pressburg of 26 December 1805 gave Baden Breisgau and other Austrian lands.
wars.note: The page names Baden among Napoleon's German allies without a date for its entry; Württemberg joined on 5 September 1805. No Baden land changed hands before the treaty.

certainty.note: The pages name lands, abbeys and cities, not boundary lines; the Lake Constance and Palatine frontiers are approximate. No survey or treaty line was opened.

notes: Cliopatria's 1803 and 1805 shapes (identical, 7,391 km2) lack the Lake Constance lands of the Bishopric of Constance, the largest single gain of 1803, so both are marked adjust with a Konstanz circle added. The 1803 gains are placed at month 4 (the Recess became law on 27 April 1803); the Recess itself is dated 25 February. Counterparts use the dossiers other agents have written (margraviate-of-baden, prince-bishopric-of-constance, -speyer and -strasbourg, electoral-palatinate via duchy-of-bavaria, further-austria); only the Schliengen/Basel lands and the imperial cities have no dossier and fall back on the Holy Roman Empire Minor States row. The further-austria dossier says Pressburg assigned the Habsburg lands to the Grand Duchy of Baden and names electorate-of-baden in its dissolve event; this dossier follows it. The Pressburg gain (Breisgau and the Ortenau lands, 26 December 1805) is recorded here with the month but belongs on the map from 1806 in the Grand Duchy's dossier; The Freiburg circle is only a rough placement of the Breisgau and the Grand Duchy agent should replace it. Small places (Bruchsal, Offenburg, Schliengen, Überlingen) are absent from the gazetteer and are given as coordinates.
